To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of relational database management systems for neuroimaging data analysis and storage can significantly improve data management efficiency and data sharing.

(a) relational database management systems (RDBMSs) provide a robust, scalable, and secure platform for data analysis, data sharing, and distributed computing in neuroimaging; (b) RDBMSs are more flexible, more secure, and more scalable for data sharing and data analysis than current solutions based on binary or text files; and (c) a combination of RDBMSs and cluster computing provides a robust platform for distributed computing in neuroinformatics.
the use of open source relational databases for the analysis, storage, and sharing of neuro-imaging data is an efficient approach that can be implemented using existing open source tools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, implementation, and evaluation of an open source framework for the analysis, storage, and sharing of large volumes of complex neuroimaging data.
the development and implementation of a database management system for neuroimaging data.

the development of a framework for the storage and analysis of neuroimaging and other biomedical data that will enable more complex research questions to be addressed, and will facilitate collaborative research and data sharing in a secure environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach presented here has the potential to revolutionize the way in which neuroimaging data are analyzed and shared, and to make it much more accessible to the broader scientific community.
this approach is superior to existing approaches for neuroimaging research.
the approach we have described here has a number of important advantages over current approaches, and that these advantages are not limited to a few specific use-cases, but are generalizable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is now feasible to use a relational database to store and analyze neuroimaging data, including time series data.
we have shown that the relational database approach is feasible and has the potential to greatly improve the way neuroimaging research is conducted.
we have shown that relational databases and distributed data processing provide an efficient and flexible approach for data analysis and sharing in the neuroimaging community.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of database management systems can significantly enhance data analysis, data sharing, and data storage in a neuroimaging environment, with minimal additional effort on the part of the researcher.

the use of relational database systems for neuroimaging data management can greatly facilitate the analysis and sharing of data, and that the use of distributed computing can greatly facilitate data analysis.
the use of relational databases for data management and analysis is an attractive alternative to the current approaches.
